label_policy: Every factual claim is tagged 'Official rule' with source URL + 'Checked Nov 9, 2026'. Gaps use 'Not stated on the official page'. No invented fees or durations.

routes.title: USA ↔ Canada with a dog or cat
routes.h1: Travelling with a dog or cat between the USA and Canada
routes.lead: Personal pets moving between the United States and Canada usually need only a valid rabies certificate to enter Canada, and the free CDC Dog Import Form (plus age and microchip rules) to return to the United States. Always confirm with CFIA and CDC before you travel.

quick.text: Dogs older than 8 months and cats entering Canada as personal pets: a current rabies vaccination certificate from a licensed vet (English or French, identifying the animal) is enough. No USDA APHIS health-certificate endorsement is required for these cases.
quick.label: Official rule
quick.source_title: USDA APHIS: Pet travel US to Canada

quick.text: Dogs 3–8 months travelling with their owner: rabies certificate if 3 months or older. Dogs under 3 months: no rabies vaccine required, but carry proof of age.
quick.label: Official rule
quick.source_title: USDA APHIS: Pet travel US to Canada

quick.text: Unaccompanied dogs under 8 months: health certificate issued by a licensed US vet within 72 hours of arrival in Canada; APHIS endorsement is not required for that certificate.
quick.label: Official rule
quick.source_title: USDA APHIS: Pet travel US to Canada

quick.text: Return to the US (dogs): Canada is not on the CDC high-risk dog-rabies list. Every dog needs the free CDC Dog Import Form receipt, must be 6 months or older, microchipped, and look healthy. The same receipt can be reused for 6 months for US↔Canada trips if the dog visits no other country.
quick.label: Official rule
quick.source_title: CDC: Dogs from rabies-free or low-risk countries

quick.text: Cats returning to the US: no federal rabies proof or USDA health certificate required; the cat must appear healthy. State and airline rules still apply.
quick.label: Official rule
quick.source_title: USDA APHIS: Cats entering the US

leaving_usa.text: Destination (Canada) sets entry rules. For most personal dogs over 8 months and for cats, APHIS does not require a VEHCS-endorsed export health certificate — only rabies proof as above.
leaving_usa.label: Official rule
leaving_usa.source_title: USDA APHIS: Pet travel US to Canada

leaving_usa.text: If a health certificate is needed (e.g. unaccompanied puppy under 8 months), a licensed US vet issues it; APHIS endorsement is not required for that Canada certificate.
leaving_usa.label: Official rule
leaving_usa.source_title: USDA APHIS: Pet travel US to Canada

leaving_usa.text: Airlines may still ask for a health/acclimation certificate within about 10 days of travel — check your airline page.
leaving_usa.label: Official rule
leaving_usa.source_title: USDA APHIS: Take a pet from the US to another country

entering_destination.text: CFIA personal dogs ≥8 months: valid rabies certificate only. No microchip and no quarantine stated for personal accompanied dogs.
entering_destination.label: Official rule
entering_destination.source_title: CFIA: Importing pets to Canada

entering_destination.text: CFIA cats ≥3 months: rabies certificate (or allowed alternatives on the CFIA page). Cats under 3 months: no CFIA restrictions stated.
entering_destination.label: Official rule
entering_destination.source_title: CFIA: Importing pets to Canada

entering_destination.text: Commercial dogs (adoption, rescue, fostering, resale, breeding, show) need an import permit; commercial dogs from CFIA high-risk countries have been prohibited since 28 Sep 2022. The US is not on that list.
entering_destination.label: Official rule
entering_destination.source_title: CFIA: Importing pets to Canada

entering_destination.text: Border checks are carried out by CBSA using CFIA rules.
entering_destination.label: Official rule
entering_destination.source_title: CBSA: Animals

entering_destination.text: Ontario and some cities (e.g. Winnipeg) restrict certain pit-bull-type breeds — separate from federal import rules.
entering_destination.label: Official rule
entering_destination.source_title: CFIA: Importing pets to Canada

return_usa.text: Since 1 Aug 2024, every dog entering or returning to the US needs the CDC Dog Import Form receipt, age ≥6 months, a microchip readable by a universal scanner, and must appear healthy.
return_usa.label: Official rule
return_usa.source_title: CDC: Bringing a dog into the United States

return_usa.text: Dogs that spent the past 6 months only in dog-rabies-free or low-risk countries (Canada is not on the CDC high-risk list) need no extra rabies document for CDC.
return_usa.label: Official rule
return_usa.source_title: CDC: Dogs from rabies-free or low-risk countries

return_usa.text: Cats: CDC/APHIS — appear healthy; no federal rabies certificate required. Confirm destination US state rules.
return_usa.label: Official rule
return_usa.source_title: USDA APHIS: Cats entering the US

exit_destination.text: CFIA/APHIS pages for personal pets returning to the US do not state a Canada exit health certificate requirement. Confirm with your airline and any provincial rules before departure.
exit_destination.label: Official rule

exit_destination.text: Complete the CDC Dog Import Form before arrival in the US and carry the receipt (and microchip reader if the chip is non-ISO).
exit_destination.label: Official rule
exit_destination.source_title: CDC: Dogs from rabies-free or low-risk countries

timeline.what: Confirm rabies vaccine is current (dogs/cats ≥3 months). Carry the original certificate in English or French.
Book a licensed-vet exam so the health certificate is issued within 72 hours of arrival in Canada.
Submit the free CDC Dog Import Form; print/save the receipt. Same receipt reusable 6 months for US↔Canada only.
Clean carrier; airline documents; arrive early for CBSA/CDC checks.

checklist_out: Rabies certificate (dogs ≥3 mo / cats ≥3 mo) — Official rule
Proof of age if dog or cat under 3 months
Health certificate ≤72 h if unaccompanied dog under 8 months
Airline pet booking + any airline health form
No APHIS VEHCS endorsement needed for typical personal adult dogs/cats (confirm your case on APHIS Canada page)
checklist_return: Cats: healthy appearance; check US state + airline

faq.q: Do I need USDA APHIS endorsement to take my adult dog to Canada?
faq.a: Usually no. APHIS states pet dogs older than 8 months and cats do not require a health certificate for Canada — only proof of rabies vaccination. Confirm your exact case on the APHIS Canada page. Checked Nov 9, 2026.

faq.q: Is Canada high-risk for dog rabies under CDC rules?
faq.a: No. Canada is not on the CDC high-risk list, so dogs that stayed only in low-risk countries need the CDC Dog Import Form, age, microchip and a healthy look — not an extra rabies titer for CDC. Checked Nov 9, 2026.

faq.q: Can the same CDC Dog Import Form receipt be reused?
faq.a: Yes for frequent US↔Canada travel for up to 6 months, unless the dog visits a different country or a high-risk country. Checked Nov 9, 2026.

gaps: No dollar amounts for CBSA/CFIA inspection fees stated on the pet pages reviewed — marked Not stated on the official page.
Ontario/Winnipeg breed rules are provincial/municipal; not a substitute for federal import rules.

routes.title: USA ↔ Mexico with a dog or cat
routes.h1: Travelling with a dog or cat between the USA and Mexico
routes.lead: Since 3 August 2026, US-origin dogs need a New World screwworm (NWS) inspection certificate signed by a USDA-accredited vet within 5 days of entry into Mexico (no APHIS endorsement). Cats still need no health certificate. Returning dogs also need a SENASICA screwworm-freedom certificate plus the CDC Dog Import Form.

quick.text: Dogs US → Mexico (since 3 Aug 2026): NWS Inspection Certificate for Pet Dogs Moving from the US to Mexico, signed by a USDA-accredited veterinarian within 5 days before entry. No APHIS endorsement. Missing or improper NWS paperwork can mean denied entry or holding at the border.
quick.label: Official rule
quick.source_title: USDA APHIS: Pet travel US to Mexico

quick.text: Cats US → Mexico: no health certificate and no NWS document since 16 Dec 2019. Do not add cats to the dog NWS form — that invalidates it.
quick.label: Official rule
quick.source_title: USDA APHIS: Pet travel US to Mexico

quick.text: At Mexico OISA (SENASICA): pet must show no disease signs, no ectoparasites, no fresh/healing wounds. Dirty bedding, toys and extra food are removed/destroyed; only that day’s food ration is allowed.
quick.label: Official rule
quick.source_title: USDA APHIS: Pet travel US to Mexico

quick.text: Return dogs Mexico → US: Mexico has been screwworm-affected since 22 Nov 2024. Every dog needs a screwworm-freedom certificate from a SENASICA-approved vet (inspection ≤5 days before travel) PLUS CDC Dog Import Form, age ≥6 months, microchip, healthy appearance.
quick.label: Official rule
quick.source_title: USDA APHIS: Dogs entering the US

quick.text: Mexico is not on the CDC high-risk dog-rabies list (low-risk for CDC rabies rules). Screwworm rules are separate USDA/SENASICA requirements.
quick.label: Official rule
quick.source_title: CDC: Dogs from rabies-free or low-risk countries

leaving_usa.text: For dogs: obtain the NWS inspection certificate from a USDA-accredited vet ≤5 days before Mexican entry. APHIS endorsement is not required for this dog form.
leaving_usa.label: Official rule
leaving_usa.source_title: USDA APHIS: Pet travel US to Mexico

leaving_usa.text: For cats: no USDA export health certificate required for Mexico entry.
leaving_usa.label: Official rule
leaving_usa.source_title: USDA APHIS: Pet travel US to Mexico

leaving_usa.text: Airlines may still require their own health/acclimation paperwork — confirm on your airline page.
leaving_usa.label: Official rule
leaving_usa.source_title: USDA APHIS: Take a pet from the US to another country

entering_destination.text: Present the dog at OISA with the NWS certificate; SENASICA issues the Certificado Zoosanitario para Importación (CZI) after inspection.
entering_destination.label: Official rule
entering_destination.source_title: SENASICA (Mexico)

entering_destination.text: Cats are inspected at OISA without a health certificate.
entering_destination.label: Official rule
entering_destination.source_title: USDA APHIS: Pet travel US to Mexico

entering_destination.text: Frequent-traveler Pet Program registration is available via SENASICA (phone numbers on the APHIS Mexico page).
entering_destination.label: Official rule
entering_destination.source_title: USDA APHIS: Pet travel US to Mexico

entering_destination.text: No federal breed import ban found in SENASICA/APHIS sources reviewed.
entering_destination.label: Official rule
entering_destination.source_title: USDA APHIS: Pet travel US to Mexico

return_usa.text: CDC (since 1 Aug 2024): Dog Import Form receipt, ≥6 months, microchip, healthy. Mexico is low-risk for CDC dog-rabies purposes if the dog was not in a high-risk country in the past 6 months.
return_usa.label: Official rule
return_usa.source_title: CDC: Dogs from rabies-free or low-risk countries

return_usa.text: USDA APHIS: screwworm-freedom certificate from a SENASICA-approved veterinarian, inspection within 5 days before shipment/travel into the US.
return_usa.label: Official rule
return_usa.source_title: USDA APHIS: Dogs entering the US

return_usa.text: Use the SENASICA directory of approved clinic veterinarians (MVRA) to find a qualifying vet in Mexico.
return_usa.label: Official rule

return_usa.text: Cats: appear healthy; no federal rabies certificate. State/airline rules may apply.
return_usa.label: Official rule
return_usa.source_title: USDA APHIS: Cats entering the US

exit_destination.text: Before leaving Mexico with a dog: book a SENASICA-approved vet for the screwworm-freedom inspection ≤5 days before US arrival.
exit_destination.label: Official rule
exit_destination.source_title: USDA APHIS: Dogs entering the US

exit_destination.text: Complete the CDC Dog Import Form listing Mexico as the departure country; a prior Canada/US-only receipt is not valid if the dog visited Mexico.
exit_destination.label: Official rule
exit_destination.source_title: CDC: Dogs from rabies-free or low-risk countries

timeline.what: USDA-accredited vet issues NWS inspection certificate (no APHIS endorsement).
Go to OISA with clean carrier; inspection; CZI issued.
SENASICA-approved vet issues screwworm-freedom certificate.
CDC Dog Import Form receipt; microchip; age ≥6 months.

checklist_out: Dogs: NWS inspection certificate ≤5 days (USDA-accredited vet, no APHIS endorsement)
Cats: no health certificate for Mexico entry
Clean carrier; only day’s food ration
Airline pet booking
checklist_return: Dogs: CDC Dog Import Form (departure country = Mexico)

faq.q: Do dogs need APHIS endorsement to enter Mexico?
faq.a: No for the NWS dog inspection certificate effective 3 Aug 2026 — a USDA-accredited vet signs it directly. Checked Nov 9, 2026 on APHIS Mexico page.

faq.q: Can I put my cat on the dog NWS form?
faq.a: No. APHIS warns that adding cats invalidates the dog form and can lead to denial or holding. Checked Nov 9, 2026.

faq.q: Is Mexico high-risk for CDC dog rabies?
faq.a: No — Mexico is not on the CDC high-risk list. Screwworm certification is a separate USDA requirement. Checked Nov 9, 2026.

gaps: Exact OISA cash fees: Not stated on the APHIS/SENASICA pages reviewed for dogs/cats.
Land-border vs airport procedural differences beyond OISA: confirm locally.

routes.title: USA ↔ United Kingdom (Great Britain) with a dog or cat
routes.h1: Travelling with a dog or cat between the USA and Great Britain
routes.lead: Great Britain requires an ISO microchip, rabies vaccination with a 21-day wait, a Great Britain pet health certificate endorsed by USDA APHIS (ink endorsement), and — for dogs — tapeworm treatment 24–120 hours before arrival. Pets may not travel in the cabin on commercial flights into GB; use an approved route. Returning to the US follows CDC low-risk rules.

quick.text: Microchip before (or same day as) rabies vaccine; rabies at ≥12 weeks; wait ≥21 full days after primary vaccination before entering GB.
quick.label: Official rule
quick.source_title: GOV.UK: Bring a pet to Great Britain

quick.text: From the US: Great Britain pet health certificate issued by a USDA-accredited vet and endorsed by APHIS. APHIS requires original ink endorsement (not digital-only). Enter GB within 10 days of the certificate (APHIS timing: arrive within 10 days of APHIS endorsement).
quick.label: Official rule
quick.source_title: USDA APHIS: Pet travel US to United Kingdom / Great Britain

quick.text: Dogs: tapeworm (praziquantel) treatment by a USDA-accredited vet 24–120 hours before entering GB, recorded on the certificate.
quick.label: Official rule
quick.source_title: GOV.UK: Tapeworm treatment for dogs

quick.text: No pets in the cabin on commercial flights into Great Britain — pets travel as cargo on approved routes (e.g. HARC at Heathrow, AAC at Gatwick, Pets on Jets at Manchester).
quick.label: Official rule
quick.source_title: GOV.UK: Travel routes for pets

quick.text: Return to the US: UK is not on the CDC high-risk list. Dogs need CDC Dog Import Form, ≥6 months, microchip, healthy look.
quick.label: Official rule
quick.source_title: CDC: Dogs from rabies-free or low-risk countries

leaving_usa.text: USDA-accredited vet completes the correct GB health certificate (non-commercial vs commercial rules) and submits via VEHCS. APHIS ink-signs and embosses; arrange prepaid return mail for the paper certificate.
leaving_usa.label: Official rule
leaving_usa.source_title: USDA APHIS: Pet travel US to United Kingdom / Great Britain

leaving_usa.text: Non-commercial certificate: typically ≤5 pets travelling within 5 days of the owner/designated person. Owner declaration on the final page must travel with the pet.
leaving_usa.label: Official rule
leaving_usa.source_title: USDA APHIS: Pet travel US to United Kingdom / Great Britain

leaving_usa.text: Schedule tapeworm treatment for dogs inside the 24–120 hour window before GB arrival.
leaving_usa.label: Official rule

entering_destination.text: Use an approved air, sea or rail route/carrier (GOV.UK list). Exception: travel from Ireland / within the UK.
entering_destination.label: Official rule
entering_destination.source_title: GOV.UK: Travel routes for pets

entering_destination.text: Non-compliance can mean quarantine up to 4 months or refusal of entry, at the owner’s cost.
entering_destination.label: Official rule
entering_destination.source_title: GOV.UK: Bring a pet to Great Britain

entering_destination.text: Banned types (Dangerous Dogs Act / XL Bully rules): Pit Bull Terrier, Japanese Tosa, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, XL Bully — cannot bring a banned type into GB without a valid Certificate of Exemption.
entering_destination.label: Official rule
entering_destination.source_title: GOV.UK: Banned dogs

entering_destination.text: Northern Ireland follows EU pet rules (DAERA), not GB rules — do not mix the two regimes.
entering_destination.label: Official rule
entering_destination.source_title: GOV.UK: Bring a pet to Great Britain

return_usa.text: CDC Dog Import Form, age ≥6 months, microchip, healthy. UK is low-risk for CDC dog-rabies purposes if no high-risk country visit in 6 months.
return_usa.label: Official rule
return_usa.source_title: CDC: Dogs from rabies-free or low-risk countries

return_usa.text: Cats: appear healthy at federal level; check airline and US state rules.
return_usa.label: Official rule
return_usa.source_title: USDA APHIS: Cats entering the US

exit_destination.text: Leaving Great Britain for a non-EU destination such as the US: follow destination (CDC/APHIS) rules. GOV.UK “taking your pet abroad” focuses on EU travel with an animal health certificate; for the US, complete the CDC Dog Import Form and confirm any APHA/export paperwork your carrier asks for.
exit_destination.label: Official rule

exit_destination.text: Not stated on the official GB pages reviewed: a mandatory GB exit health certificate solely for return to the US. Confirm with APHA Pet Travel helpline and your airline before departure.
exit_destination.label: Official rule

timeline.what: ISO microchip, then rabies vaccine.
Earliest GB entry after primary rabies (day of vaccine = day 0 per APHIS UK wording).
USDA-accredited vet issues GB PHC; submit VEHCS; wait for APHIS ink endorsement; book approved cargo route.
Tapeworm treatment recorded on certificate.
Arrive in Great Britain.
CDC Dog Import Form receipt.

checklist_out: ISO microchip before/with rabies
Rabies + 21-day wait
GB pet health certificate + APHIS ink endorsement (VEHCS)
Dogs: tapeworm 24–120 h before arrival
Approved route / cargo booking (no cabin on commercial flights into GB)
Owner declaration signed
checklist_return: Confirm any APHA/export docs airline requires

faq.q: Can my dog fly in the cabin to London?
faq.a: Not on commercial flights into Great Britain for ordinary pets. GOV.UK requires approved routes; pets typically travel as cargo to designated centres. Assistance dogs have separate rules. Checked Nov 9, 2026.

faq.q: Does APHIS digitally endorse UK certificates?
faq.a: No — APHIS states original ink endorsement is required for GB. Plan mailing time. Checked Nov 9, 2026.
No. Tapeworm treatment applies to dogs (with listed exemptions for certain countries). Checked Nov 9, 2026.

gaps: No dedicated live PPC country page for the UK yet (404 on /countries/uk.html).
No live USA↔UK overview route page; only UK→France airline pages and other corridors exist.
Exact cargo centre fees: Not stated as a single official amount on GOV.UK bring-pet pages reviewed.

routes.title: USA ↔ Japan with a dog or cat
routes.h1: Travelling with a dog or cat between the USA and Japan
routes.lead: Japan treats the US mainland (except Hawaii and Guam) as a non-designated region: ISO microchip, two rabies shots, a rabies titer ≥0.5 IU/ml, then a 180-day wait, plus 40-day advance notice to AQS. USDA APHIS endorses the health certificate digitally for dogs/cats to Japan. Returning to the US follows CDC low-risk rules; leaving Japan needs an AQS export inspection.

quick.text: US mainland dogs & cats: ISO microchip, two rabies vaccinations, rabies titer ≥0.5 IU/ml at an approved lab, 180-day wait after the blood draw, AQS notification ≥40 days before arrival, vet exam within 10 days before boarding, government-endorsed certificate. Quarantine then within 12 hours if compliant.
quick.label: Official rule
quick.source_title: Japan AQS: Import from non-designated regions

quick.text: Health certificate: Form AC (or alternatives) by USDA-accredited vet via VEHCS; APHIS digitally endorses dog/cat certificates to Japan — carry a printed copy.
quick.label: Official rule
quick.source_title: USDA APHIS: Pet travel US to Japan

quick.text: Hawaii/Guam (designated): no titer/180-day wait; residence rules, Form AB, 40-day notice.
quick.label: Official rule
quick.source_title: Japan AQS: Import from designated regions

quick.text: Return to US: Japan not on CDC high-risk list — CDC Dog Import Form, ≥6 months, microchip, healthy.
quick.label: Official rule
quick.source_title: CDC: Dogs from rabies-free or low-risk countries

quick.text: Leaving Japan: dogs and cats need an AQS export inspection; AQS asks you to apply at least 14 days before departure.
quick.label: Official rule
quick.source_title: Japan AQS: Import from non-designated regions

leaving_usa.text: USDA-accredited vet prepares Form AC (or Form A+C / 7001+A) and submits through VEHCS for digital APHIS endorsement; print and carry the endorsed certificate.
leaving_usa.label: Official rule
leaving_usa.source_title: USDA APHIS: Pet travel US to Japan

leaving_usa.text: Vet exam within 10 days before boarding confirming no rabies signs (and for dogs, leptospirosis) and microchip check.
leaving_usa.label: Official rule
leaving_usa.source_title: Japan AQS: Import from non-designated regions

entering_destination.text: Microchip ISO 11784/11785 before or same day as first rabies shot. Chips starting 900 202 not accepted for now.
entering_destination.label: Official rule
entering_destination.source_title: Japan AQS: Import from non-designated regions

entering_destination.text: First rabies ≥91 days old; second ≥30 days later within DOI; inactivated/recombinant only.
entering_destination.label: Official rule
entering_destination.source_title: Japan AQS: Import from non-designated regions

entering_destination.text: FAVN/titer after second shot at Japan-approved lab; ≥0.5 IU/ml; valid 2 years from blood draw. APHIS lists KSU Rabies Lab and DOD VFADL among US labs.
entering_destination.label: Official rule
entering_destination.source_title: USDA APHIS: Pet travel US to Japan

entering_destination.text: Arrive ≥180 days after blood draw (draw = day 0). Early arrival = quarantine for missing days.
entering_destination.label: Official rule
entering_destination.source_title: Japan AQS: Import from non-designated regions

entering_destination.text: Notify AQS ≥40 days ahead (NACCS or email). Dogs enter only through designated ports (Narita, Haneda, Kansai, etc.).
entering_destination.label: Official rule
entering_destination.source_title: Japan AQS: Import from non-designated regions

entering_destination.text: If requirements not met: detention up to 180 days at owner’s cost, or ship back.
entering_destination.label: Official rule
entering_destination.source_title: Japan AQS: Import from non-designated regions

return_usa.text: CDC Dog Import Form, ≥6 months, microchip, healthy; Japan low-risk for CDC if no high-risk visit in 6 months.
return_usa.label: Official rule
return_usa.source_title: CDC: Dogs from rabies-free or low-risk countries

return_usa.text: Cats: appear healthy federally; state/airline rules apply.
return_usa.label: Official rule
return_usa.source_title: USDA APHIS: Cats entering the US

exit_destination.text: Apply to AQS for export inspection at least 14 days before departure from Japan.
exit_destination.label: Official rule
exit_destination.source_title: Japan AQS: Import from non-designated regions

exit_destination.text: Keep the import quarantine certificate — AQS notes it cannot be reissued and is needed to leave Japan.
exit_destination.label: Official rule
exit_destination.source_title: Japan AQS: Import from non-designated regions

exit_destination.text: Dogs: register with city/town within 30 days of arrival and keep annual rabies vaccination while in Japan.
exit_destination.label: Official rule
exit_destination.source_title: Japan AQS: Import from non-designated regions

timeline.what: ISO microchip → first rabies (≥91 days old).
Second rabies → blood draw for titer (same day as 2nd shot allowed).
Receive titer ≥0.5 IU/ml (result valid 2 years from draw).
Earliest arrival in Japan without extra quarantine days.
Notify AQS; obtain approval.
Vet exam; VEHCS certificate; APHIS digital endorsement; print copy.
Apply for AQS export inspection; complete CDC form for US return.

checklist_out: ISO microchip timing correct vs first rabies
Two rabies shots (inactivated/recombinant)
Approved-lab titer ≥0.5 IU/ml + 180-day wait
AQS advance notice ≥40 days
Vet exam ≤10 days + APHIS-endorsed Form AC (printed)
Arrive via designated dog port

faq.q: How early should I start for Japan?
faq.a: By AQS timing, after first shot (≥91 days old), second shot ≥30 days later, then 180 days after the titer blood draw — roughly 7+ months before arrival for a mainland US pet. Checked Nov 9, 2026.

faq.q: Is APHIS endorsement digital for Japan?
faq.a: Yes for dog and cat certificates to Japan per APHIS; still carry a printed endorsed copy. Checked Nov 9, 2026.

faq.q: What if I arrive before day 180?
faq.a: AQS holds the pet for the missing days (up to 180) at your cost, or the pet may be returned. Checked Nov 9, 2026.

gaps: Live overview page already exists at /routes/usa-to-japan.html (checked Oct 24, 2026 on live). This pack refreshes to Checked Nov 9, 2026 and adds explicit return/exit checklist structure for the country-pair series.
AQS import inspection fee amount: Not stated on AQS dog/cat import pages.

routes.title: USA ↔ France (EU) with a dog or cat
routes.h1: Travelling with a dog or cat between the USA and France
routes.lead: France follows EU pet-entry rules: ISO microchip before rabies, rabies at ≥12 weeks with a 21-day wait, and an EU animal health certificate issued by a USDA-accredited vet and ink-endorsed by APHIS. The US is a listed third country — no rabies titer. New EU non-commercial certificates took effect 1 October 2026. Category 1 dogs are banned from import and transit.

quick.text: ISO 11784/11785 microchip implanted before or on the same day as rabies vaccination; rabies at ≥12 weeks; wait ≥21 days after primary vaccination.
quick.label: Official rule
quick.source_title: USDA APHIS: Pet travel US to France

quick.text: US is listed → no rabies antibody titer required for entry into the EU/France from the US.
quick.label: Official rule
quick.source_title: European Commission: Entry of dogs, cats and ferrets into the Union

quick.text: Non-commercial EU health certificate: USDA-accredited vet issues; APHIS original ink endorsement required. Endorsement must fall within 10 days of arrival in the EU. New non-commercial certificates effective 1 Oct 2026 (EU 2026/131 & 2026/848).
quick.label: Official rule
quick.source_title: USDA APHIS: Pet travel US to France

quick.text: Max 5 pets for non-commercial movement; written non-commercial declaration; documents in French (or bilingual / sworn translation) when presenting in France.
quick.label: Official rule
quick.source_title: Service-Public.fr: Importation d'un animal de compagnie

quick.text: Catégorie 1 dogs (certain non-LOF morphotypes): import AND transit into France prohibited. Catégorie 2 allowed only with French paperwork.
quick.label: Official rule
quick.source_title: Ministère de l'Agriculture: Chiens de catégorie 1 et 2

quick.text: Return to US: France not on CDC high-risk list — CDC Dog Import Form, ≥6 months, microchip, healthy.
quick.label: Official rule
quick.source_title: CDC: Dogs from rabies-free or low-risk countries

leaving_usa.text: Choose non-commercial vs commercial EU certificate per APHIS France page. Non-commercial: owner or designated person within 5 days, ≤5 pets (event exceptions exist).
leaving_usa.label: Official rule
leaving_usa.source_title: USDA APHIS: Pet travel US to France

leaving_usa.text: Submit via VEHCS; APHIS ink-signs and embosses; prepaid return label needed. Carry original endorsed paper certificate + owner declaration.
leaving_usa.label: Official rule
leaving_usa.source_title: USDA APHIS: Pet travel US to France

leaving_usa.text: Primary US rabies for EU purposes is valid 1 year even if a 3-year product was used; keep continuous booster history without gaps.
leaving_usa.label: Official rule
leaving_usa.source_title: USDA APHIS: Pet travel US to France

entering_destination.text: Present spontaneously to French customs at a travellers’ point of entry; no import permit for compliant non-commercial pets.
entering_destination.label: Official rule
entering_destination.source_title: Service-Public.fr: Importation d'un animal de compagnie

entering_destination.text: Dogs from third countries must have at least one adult tooth (Code rural).

faq.q: Do I need a rabies titer for France from the US?
faq.a: No. The US is a listed third country for EU pet entry; titer applies to unlisted/high-risk third countries. Checked Nov 9, 2026.

APHIS requires new EU non-commercial health certificates effective 1 Oct 2026 (commercial model 17 Oct 2026) under EU 2026/131 and 2026/848. Old certificates in process could be endorsed only through 30 Sep 2026. Checked Nov 9, 2026.

faq.q: Can a pit-bull-type dog transit France to another country?
faq.a: Catégorie 1 morphotype dogs: French law bans import and transit. Do not plan a French connection for those dogs. Checked Nov 9, 2026.
